home.title: Describe your project and get the concrete recipe that fits it.
home.lead: One sentence is enough: what you build, where it stands, how big it is. CreteLab reads the requirements, calculates the recipe after Zement-Merkblatt B 20 and tells you whether bags, mixing it yourself or ready-mixed concrete fits best.
home.privacy: Your description is analysed, not stored. The language model runs on our own server.

needs.headline: {volume} of {strength} concrete

reason.x0: X0: unreinforced, no frost, no wear, so no attack.
reason.xc2: XC2: reinforced, permanently wet or in contact with the ground.
reason.xc3: XC3: reinforced, moderately humid, sheltered from rain.
reason.xc4: XC4: reinforced, wet and dry in turn from rain.
reason.xd1: XD1: reinforced, spray containing de-icing salt.
reason.xd2: XD2: reinforced, permanently wet with chlorides.
reason.xd3: XD3: reinforced, de-icing salt on a horizontal surface.
reason.xf1: XF1: frost without de-icing agents, vertical surface.
reason.xf2: XF2: frost with de-icing agents, vertical surface.
reason.xf3: XF3: frost without de-icing agents, horizontal surface.
reason.xf4: XF4: frost with de-icing agents, horizontal surface.
reason.xm2: XM2: heavy wear from trucks or forklifts.
reason.xs1: XS1: salty air from the sea.
reason.lp: Air-entraining agent: tiny air bubbles give freezing water room to expand.
reason.wu: Waterproofing admixture and at least C25/30 for watertight concrete (WU-Richtlinie).

order.name: Ready-mixed concrete
order.sub: from a plant, from about 1 m³

bag.yield: about {litres} l of fresh concrete per bag
bag.example: An example. Any product with the same declared classes works just as well.
bag.notPossible: Bagged concrete does not work here.

issue.watertight: Watertight (WU): no bagged concrete is declared as watertight, and waterproofing admixtures are no substitute. Order watertight ready-mixed concrete for basements and tanks.
issue.notDeclared: No bagged concrete is declared for {classes}. Mix it yourself or order ready-mixed concrete.
issue.tradeOnly: Only a trade product from builders' merchants meets the requirements: {product}. DIY stores rarely stock it.
issue.tooThin: Too thin: {thicknessMm} mm walls. Bagged concrete with 8 mm aggregate needs at least {minMm} mm; the largest grain may be at most a third of the thickness.
issue.manyBags: About {bags} bags, a lot to carry and mix. A concrete mixer pays off.
issue.orderInstead: About {bags} bags: from about 1 m³, ready-mixed concrete or a self-service concrete station is usually easier and cheaper.

rule.water-as-stated: Add only as much water as the bag says. More water lowers the strength, and the declared classes no longer apply.
rule.no-additions: Add nothing but water: manufacturers explicitly rule out additions such as cement, waterproofing or air-entraining agents.
rule.temperature: Work only between +5 and +30 °C and keep the concrete moist for a few days.

bag.asksForAdditions: You want to add something to the ready mix: manufacturers forbid it, and the classes on the bag then no longer apply. To see what it would change anyway, open

error.fmRequired: Consistency {consistency} needs a superplasticiser (FM). Choose one under “Adjust details”.

mix.largeVolume: Mixing {volume} yourself is a lot of work. From about 1 m³ ready-mixed concrete is usually cheaper, see the “Ready-mixed concrete” tab.

warning.strength-below-exposure: {strengthClass} is too weak for the chosen exposure classes: at least {minFckCube} N/mm² cube strength is required.
warning.wz-exceeded: The w/c ratio {wz} is above the limit {maxWz} of the exposure classes.
warning.fines-too-high: Fines content {fines} kg/m³ is too high; {max} kg/m³ is allowed (DIN 1045-2).
warning.fly-ash-with-silica-fume: Too much fly ash next to silica fume for CEM I: f/c ≤ 3 · (0.22 − s/c).
warning.high-air: {airPct} % air is unusually high and costs a lot of strength.

row.silicaFumeNote: fills the finest pores, denser and stronger
row.aggregateNote: sand and gravel, the skeleton of the concrete

row.fmNote: saves about 20 % water, makes it flowable

calc.water: Water demand from grading and consistency: {water} l/m³.
calc.wzStrength: The w/c from the Walz curve, {walz}, is stricter than the exposure limit ({exposure}): w/c = {wz}.
calc.volumes: Absolute volumes in dm³: cement {cement} + water {water} + fly ash {flyAsh} + silica fume {silicaFume} + waterproofing {waterproofing} + air {air} + aggregate {aggregate} = 1000.
calc.added: Water {water} l/m³, of which {added} l/m³ to add.
calc.source: Method and tables: Zement-Merkblatt B 20 (2.2017), Walz curves digitised from its Bild 1. The calculation is tested against the leaflet's worked examples I to IV.

step.mix: Mix well until the consistency is {consistency}.
step.place: Place it within about 30 minutes, compact it and keep it moist for a few days.

order.lead: A plant sells concrete by its properties. It needs these details; the mix design is the plant's job.
order.small: {volume} is little for a truck mixer: plants charge a small-quantity surcharge. Compare with bags or mixing it yourself, or look for a self-service concrete station.

moistureClass.WA: wet with salt from outside (de-icing salt, sea)
moistureClass.WS: like WA, plus heavy traffic loads

tip.volume: Order {volume}: rounded up to half a cubic metre, with a little allowance for loss.
tip.surcharge: Below 3–6 m³ per delivery many plants charge a small-quantity surcharge of about €23–35 per missing m³.
tip.station: For small amounts from about 0.15 m³ there are self-service concrete stations where you collect it with a trailer.
tip.noWater: Do not add water: the plant is no longer liable for the concrete if you do.

decor.thickWall: From about 6 cm wall thickness ordinary concrete pays off:

row.quartzNote: fills the gaps between the grains

pce.error: outside 0.3–4.0 %, a different superplasticiser is needed

diy-pce-30l-batch.label: Fine mortar for furniture (quartz sand and quartz flour)
diy-pce-30l-batch.use: For tables, benches and pots with 1–2.5 cm walls; in a mixer.

steps.title: Pre-mix the dry ingredients for 1–2 minutes
steps.text: ({cement} cement + {sand} sand + {quartz} quartz flour). The sand is sand 0–2 mm and quartz sand 0.063–0.3 mm in a 30 : 9 ratio.

steps.title: Add about 80% of the water
steps.text: and keep mixing.

steps.title: Dissolve the PCE superplasticizer in the remaining water
steps.text: ({pce} PCE, {water} water in total) and add it — mix for at least 20 minutes in total (free-fall mixer). Some cements need a little more water.

steps.title: Pour into oiled form and vibrate
steps.text: or tap gently until no more air bubbles rise. For walls of 1–2.5 cm with textile reinforcement.

steps.title: Cover and keep moist for at least 24 h
steps.text: , carefully demold, let cure for several days.

diy-mortar-20kg-batch.label: High-strength mortar (limestone flour and microsilica)
diy-mortar-20kg-batch.use: For fine, dense surfaces and small, strong parts.

steps.title: Mix cement, dry sand and fines with about one third of the mixing water
steps.text: ({cement} cement + {sand} sand + {fines} limestone flour + {microsilica} microsilica + about one third of {water} water). Sand must be dry.

steps.title: Dissolve PCE superplasticizer in the remaining water
steps.text: ({pce} PCE in the remaining approx. two thirds of the water).

steps.title: Add the water-PCE mixture in stages and mix vigorously for at least 5 minutes
steps.text: — ideally in a forced-action mixer. The superplasticizer only reaches full effect after even distribution.

steps.title: Pour into oiled form and vibrate
steps.text: or tap gently until no more air bubbles rise.

steps.title: Cover and keep moist for at least 24 h
steps.text: , carefully demold, let cure for several days.

kassel-m1q-cem42-5r.label: Research UHPC, full superplasticiser dose
kassel-m1q-cem42-5r.use: Laboratory recipe from the University of Kassel: very strong, needs an industrial superplasticiser and a pan mixer.

steps.title: Thoroughly homogenize the dry mix
steps.text: {cement} cement + {sand} sand (0.125–0.5 mm) + {microsilica} microsilica + {quartz} quartz flour. For UHPC, mixing the fine powders evenly is critical — mix dry for at least 2 minutes.

steps.title: Dissolve PCE superplasticizer in the mixing water
steps.text: ({pce} PCE in {water} water).

steps.title: Add the water-PCE mixture in stages to the dry mix
steps.text: and mix vigorously for 5–10 minutes total — ideally in a forced-action mixer. Warning: Fresh concrete temperature can rise to 40 °C in large batches — the mix will stiffen faster.

steps.title: Pour into oiled form and compact with a standard immersion vibrator
steps.text: until the concrete levels itself.

steps.title: Demold after 24–48 hours
steps.text: (depending on superplasticizer retardation), then keep covered moist for at least one week (e.g. under wet cloth + plastic wrap). Compressive strength after 28 d: approx. 100 N/mm².

steps.title: Optional for maximum strength
steps.text: Store completely underwater at 20 °C for 28 days → ~123 N/mm² (+23%). With this very dense mix, the water bath effect is particularly strong against self-drying of the matrix.

kassel-m1q-cem42-5r-soft.label: Research UHPC, moderate superplasticiser dose (indoors)
kassel-m1q-cem42-5r-soft.use: The same recipe with a usual retail amount of superplasticiser, for indoor use.

steps.title: Thoroughly homogenize the dry mix
steps.text: {cement} cement + {sand} sand (0.125–0.5 mm) + {microsilica} microsilica + {quartz} quartz flour. Mix dry for at least 2 minutes — fine powder distribution determines final strength.

steps.title: Dissolve PCE superplasticizer in the mixing water
steps.text: ({pce} PCE in {water} water). This variant works with a DIY-typical PCE dosage.

steps.title: Add the water-PCE mixture in stages to the dry mix
steps.text: and mix for 5–10 minutes. Flow properties develop slowly — initially "grainy", then smooth after a few minutes.

steps.title: Pour into oiled form and compact with a standard immersion vibrator
steps.text: until the surface shines.

steps.title: Demold after 24–48 h
steps.text: , then keep covered moist for at least one week. Compressive strength after 28 d: approx. 95 N/mm².

steps.title: Optional for maximum strength
steps.text: Store completely underwater at 20 °C for 28 days → ~103 N/mm² (+8%). With this slightly less dense variant (w/c = 0.40), the water bath effect is smaller but noticeable.

diy-white-15kg-laminate.label: White concrete for thin-walled furniture and pots, outdoors
diy-white-15kg-laminate.use: Spray the first coat, then build it up by hand with glass-fibre mesh; weatherproof once sealed.

steps.title: Dry-mix white cement, sand and quartz flour
steps.text: ({cement} White Cement + {sand} sand + {quartz} quartz flour). The sand is sand 0–2 mm and quartz sand 0.063–0.3 mm in a 3 : 5 ratio.

steps.title: Add water and superplasticizer
steps.text: ({water} water, {pce} plasticizing superplasticizer) and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Spray a first coat of 1.5–2 mm onto the mould
steps.text: until the mould no longer shows through – this makes the visible side smooth.

steps.title: Apply further layers by hand
steps.text: – the concrete must be kneadable for this – and lay three layers of glass-fibre mesh in between.

steps.title: Let it harden for 24–48 hours
steps.text: (depending on room temperature), demould, and seal with impregnation and wax for outdoor use.

diy-white-bowl-4kg.label: White concrete for small decorative pieces (hand-mixed)
diy-white-bowl-4kg.use: For small batches up to about 5 l, with fibres and mesh.

steps.title: Dry-mix white cement and sand
steps.text: ({cement} White Cement + {sand} sand). The sand is sand 0–2 mm and quartz sand 0.063–0.3 mm in a 1 : 2 ratio.

steps.title: Add the water with the superplasticizer and the fibres
steps.text: ({water} water, {pce} high-performance superplasticizer, {fibres} reinforcing fibres) and mix thoroughly by hand.

steps.title: Fill the mould and lay in reinforcing mesh
steps.text: (cut to the shape of the mould).

steps.title: Demould after about 48 hours
steps.text: and seal with impregnation and wax.

bagTool.title: Adjust a ready mix
bagTool.lead: What more cement, fly ash, silica fume or a plasticiser would do to a bag of ready mix, estimated on the Walz curve.
bagTool.warning: Manufacturers forbid adding anything but water to ready mix. With additions, the strength and exposure classes on the bag no longer apply. Do not use it for load-bearing or standardised parts.
bagTool.mixHint: Assumed composition; datasheets do not state the cement content.

flyAsh.name: Fly ash (15 % of cement)
flyAsh.effect: less heat, denser in the long run

air.name: Air-entraining agent
air.effect: more frost resistant, costs about 14 N/mm²

waterproofing.name: Waterproofing admixture (2 % of cement)
waterproofing.effect: absorbs less water, does not make it watertight concrete

bagTool.airWithSilica: Air entrainment and silica fume do not go well together: the mix gets stiff and the air voids form poorly. Choose one of them.
bagTool.strength: {base} becomes an estimated {tuned} (about {fck} N/mm² cube strength).
